help.send-sign-in.note1: Turned on “Unlock with fingerprint or face” on this phone? The sign-in screen offers it first, and “Use my PIN instead” is one tap away. Changing your PIN turns it off on every phone.
help.follow-shop-order.title: Follow a parcel you bought from a shop
help.follow-shop-order.summary: We do not text you about a parcel. Sign up with the phone number you gave the shop, and the parcel shows in your account.
help.follow-shop-order.step1: On the shop’s page, once you have the delivery price, tap “Sign up to follow it”. It opens the Send app in a new tab; your checkout stays where it is.
help.follow-shop-order.step2: Type your phone number — the same one you give the shop — then the code we send you, and choose a 5-digit PIN. The first time, you also add a recovery email.
help.follow-shop-order.step3: Open My parcels. When the shop has sent your parcel it is there: where it is now, when it is ready, and the code to show at the counter.
help.follow-shop-order.note1: It does not matter which comes first. Sign up before the shop sends it and it appears when they do; sign up afterwards and it is already waiting.
help.follow-shop-order.note2: Nothing there? Check which number the shop has for you. A parcel sent to another number is in the account on that number, not in yours.
help.follow-shop-order.note3: For a store: the invitation is part of the shipping widget and appears under the price by itself. It works because your shipment carries the buyer’s mobile number.
help.business-sign-in.title: Sign in to the Business app
help.business-sign-in.summary: Everyone in a business signs in as themselves, with their own phone number and PIN — the same PIN as in any SeeBuyGet app.
help.business-sign-in.step1: Open the Business app from the front page: “Sign in › A business”.
help.business-sign-in.step2: Type your phone number and your 5-digit PIN. New here, or forgot your PIN? Tap “New here? Sign up” or “Forgot your PIN?”: we send a code to your phone first.
help.business-sign-in.step3: A phone or browser you have not signed in on before, or have not used for 90 days, asks for a code first: we send it to your number, you type it once, and from then on your PIN works there. Your PIN is not changed by it.
help.business-sign-in.step4: The first time, sign up your business, one step to a screen: the business (its registered name, country and registration number), what it does, and you. Then it is saved, with you as its owner, and it works. Next come its registration certificate and your ID, each by “Take a photo” or “Choose a photo or PDF”, and the ask for SeeBuyGet’s check: any of them can wait for the start screen.
help.business-sign-in.step5: In more than one business? Pick one. Switch business, in the menu under your name, takes you back to the list.
help.business-sign-in.note1: New here? Have this phone with you, and an email address you can open now: the first time, a code is sent to it too. The bar at the top of the screen names the step you are on and the one after it — tap it to see them all: your phone number, the code, your PIN, and your email address.
help.business-sign-in.note2: Turned on “Unlock with fingerprint or face” on this phone? The sign-in screen offers it first, and “Use my PIN instead” is one tap away. Changing your PIN turns it off on every phone.
help.business-check.title: How SeeBuyGet checks a business
help.business-check.summary: A business works from the moment it is set up. It is shown to others — a public page, a place in the agent finder — once two members of SeeBuyGet staff have checked it.
help.business-check.step1: Signing up, straight after the business is saved: its registration certificate, then the ID of the person speaking for it — each by “Take a photo” or “Choose a photo or PDF” — then “Ask SeeBuyGet to check us”. Each of them can wait.
help.business-check.step2: Left for later? The start screen keeps “SeeBuyGet’s check”: the same two buttons for each paper, then “Ask SeeBuyGet to check us”.
help.business-check.step3: Refused? The business reads the reason in its app and by email, puts it right, and asks again.
help.electronic-note.title: How the electronic consignment note works
help.electronic-note.summary: Every load carries its consignment note electronically. Using it, the sender, the carrier and the receiver agree to these procedures: how it is made out and handed over, how it stays as signed, who reads it, how delivery is confirmed, how it is added to, and how it is replaced by paper.
help.electronic-note.step1: Made out and handed over: the sender confirms the note by posting the load, from its own sign-in. The carrier confirms it at taking over, after the load-safety check, from the driver’s own phone. Each party opens it in its own app, and the sender is emailed a link to it when the goods are delivered.
help.electronic-note.step2: Kept as signed: at every signature and every remark — taking over, a reload, a seal changed, delivery, a refusal, a claim — the note is frozen as a new copy with a fingerprint of its own. A frozen copy is never changed. Anybody can check a printed copy against its fingerprint, at the address printed at its foot.
help.electronic-note.step3: Who reads it: the sender and the carrier — the driver and the driver’s fleet — read the whole note, by their own sign-in; a load number alone opens nothing. The business the goods are delivered to reads the receiver’s copy, without the carriage price unless the carriage is theirs to pay.
help.electronic-note.step4: Delivery confirmed: at the door the driver records the receiver’s name, a photo of the goods as delivered, and anything the receiver found not as the note says, written beside their name. That confirmation is frozen into a new copy.
help.electronic-note.step5: Added to, never rewritten: a later instruction from the sender is added with its date, and the carrier’s reservations are added where they arise. Each addition is a new copy; the earlier copies stay readable as they were.
help.electronic-note.step6: Replaced by paper when paper is asked for: print the note from the app. On paper it asks which original it is — the sender’s, the one that travels with the goods, or the carrier’s — and has a line under each confirmation for a signature by hand. Its fingerprint ties it to the electronic copy it was printed from.
help.electronic-note.note1: Which law: the note says which law the carriage is under, from where the goods are taken over and where they are delivered — the CMR when either country is a party to it, the Northern Corridor’s road protocol between its member states, and otherwise its contract and the national law that governs it.
help.electronic-note.note2: An electronic note stands as the CMR note only between countries that are parties to the e-CMR Protocol of 2008 — today mostly in Europe, none in Africa. Elsewhere it is the record the parties agreed, and a printed note signed by hand is made from it where one is asked for.
help.business-check.note1: Changing the business’s name or registration number puts it back to not checked: those are what was checked.
help.business-check.note2: The ID of the person speaking for the business is deleted the moment staff verify or refuse it. The registration certificate is kept: it is the business’s record.
help.business-check.note3: “Take a photo” opens the phone’s own camera: lay the paper flat, in good light, with all four corners in view. A photo is made smaller on the phone before it is sent; a PDF can be up to 8 MB. At a desk, both buttons open the computer’s files.
help.parcel-problem.title: Report a problem with a parcel
help.parcel-problem.summary: Broken, opened or wrong goods are reported with a photograph: by the receiver from the Send app, or by the shop at its counter. SeeBuyGet does not judge a claim or pay one. It makes a damage claim report on the spot — the record of who held the parcel and when, with the photographs — for the claimant to hand to an insurer.
help.parcel-problem.step1: Send app, after collecting: My parcels, open the parcel, “Got your parcel? › Report a problem”. Say what is wrong and add a photograph. The parcel stays “Delivered”, and a “Damage claim report” appears on it.
help.parcel-problem.step2: Shop app, at the counter, before handing over: “Hand over a parcel › Report a problem instead”. Say what is wrong and take a photograph. The report is made at once, the parcel stays in its slot, and it can still be handed over: the customer decides whether to take it.
help.parcel-problem.step3: On the parcel in the Send app, the receiver has three things under “Damage claim report”: “Read the report”; “Download the report and its photographs”, which is the copy to keep; and “Make a link to pass on”, for an insurer, the sender or the store. A link opens the report with nobody signed in, works for 30 days, and can be stopped there at any time.
help.parcel-problem.step4: The receiver and the sender each get a notice. A shop that reported it gets a notice naming the slot the parcel is in. SeeBuyGet staff see every report made and can download one; they decide nothing on it.
help.parcel-problem.step5: Store app: a report on one of your orders is listed under Orders, and opens the order, where the report is with the same three things. Under “My store › What the buyer pays › Change”, name your insurer and their email address for claims: every report on one of your shipments is then emailed there as a link, the moment it is made, and the list says where each went.
help.parcel-problem.note1: A store’s order is made only with a photograph of what is in the box, which the store keeps: it is on the order under Orders, and in the report as the “before” the problem is set against.
help.parcel-problem.note2: Every photograph in a report is one SeeBuyGet holds, taken by whoever did that step — the shop at its counter, the driver on the load, the receiver in the Send app — for that step alone. A step whose photo did not reach us is refused, and says so, so the photo is taken again while it still can be; with no signal, the app keeps the photo and sends it before the step.
help.parcel-problem.note3: The report says what the record held when the problem was reported: the parcel as it was made, every hand it passed through and when, each recorded step with its fingerprint, the photographs, and the terms it travelled under. It names shops and carriers as companies, never a person, and it carries a fingerprint of its own so two copies can be compared.
help.parcel-problem.note4: The report is the receiver’s to pass on, and a copy is the sender’s: the sender finds it on the parcel in their own Send app — to read, to download, and to pass on with a link of their own — and is told when it is made. A store reads the report on its own order.
help.parcel-problem.note5: One parcel has one report, and after the parcel is handed over it does not change: that is where the network’s part ended. What the receiver finds afterwards — goods broken inside a box that arrived whole — is added under “Found something after it was handed over?” as a dated note beside the report, with a photograph if they have one. Each note has its own fingerprint, is in the file and in every link, and says it is outside SeeBuyGet’s jurisdiction: how goods were packed is for the sender to answer. The sender is told a note was added.
help.parcel-problem.note6: Nobody is texted about a report or its outcome. Somebody without the Send app reads it on the parcel the day they sign in with the number the parcel was addressed to.
help.parcel-problem.note7: A company that carries parcels pays a claim from its own books only where it has stated cover, and no company can state cover yet. Where one has, a claim waits under Damage claims for staff to decide, with a written reason, up to the cover stated.
help.size-price.title: See why a big, light parcel costs more
help.size-price.summary: A parcel is priced by its weight or by its size, whichever is more. A big, light box takes room in the bag that nothing else can use, so by its size it counts as heavier than it weighs — and the road part of its price follows what it counts as. Under the price, the Send app and the Store app say which of the two set it.
help.size-price.step1: Measure the box from the outside, in centimetres: its length, its width and its height. Weigh it, in kilograms. The Send app and the Store app ask for all four before they show a price.
help.size-price.step2: SeeBuyGet works out what the box counts as by its size: length × width × height, divided by 7,875. A box of 45 × 35 × 25 cm counts as 5 kg.
help.size-price.step3: The price is set by whichever is more: what the box weighs, or what it counts as by its size. Under the price it says which — for example: Priced by its size, it counts as 7.6 kg and weighs 6 kg.
help.size-price.step4: The road part of the price is: the kilometres it travels × a driver’s rate per kilometre × what the box counts as, divided by 5. A box that counts as 5 kg pays the rate once for every kilometre; one that counts as 7.6 kg, 1.52 times; one that counts as 2 kg, 0.4 times. The fees of the shops and any hub on the way are the same whatever its size.
help.size-price.note1: An example: a box of 50 × 40 × 30 cm counts as 7.6 kg by its size. If it weighs 6 kg it is priced as 7.6 kg; if it weighs 9 kg, as 9 kg.
help.size-price.note2: At a shop counter a parcel is not measured: the shop picks its size — small, medium, large or heavy — and the price is that size’s. Measure it yourself in the Send app, and a smaller box costs less.
help.size-price.note3: The rate per kilometre is set by each driver for their own vehicle: what a 5 kg medium box pays to travel one kilometre. The price is worked out from the rates of the vehicles that can carry the parcel, near the shop it starts from when that is asked. The Send app’s price and the Store app’s Cheapest use the cheapest of those rates; the Store app’s Fastest uses the dearest, so any of those vehicles may take it. Where no driver has set a rate yet, the company’s own road rate is used. The driver who carries the bag is paid the kilometres × their own rate × what the parcels in it were charged as — the same count, so nobody is paid for room that was not charged.
help.size-price.note4: Why 7,875: it is the weight SeeBuyGet’s own medium size allows for its room — 45 × 35 × 25 cm, up to 5 kg — so a medium box counts the same by its size as by its weight. Many carriers divide by 5,000 or 6,000, which makes the same box count as heavier.
help.size-price.note5: A parcel is never charged more than a whole bag, the most one parcel can take on the network; its price then says it is priced as a whole bag. A box too big for a bag is not a parcel: it goes as a load, priced by the vehicle that carries it.
help.parcel-problem.note8: The email to an insurer carries a link, never the file: it opens the report for whoever holds the email, for thirty days, and the store sees that link on the report and can stop it.
help.when-to-change.title: When to change a password, PIN or key
help.when-to-change.summary: We never make you change a password or PIN on a schedule — that only makes people pick weaker ones. Change one when it matters.
help.when-to-change.step1: Change it if somebody may have seen it, if you shared it, or if you lost a phone that was signed in.
help.when-to-change.step2: Secrets that machines use — a store’s signing secret, a fleet code, a secret API key — are worth changing every 90 days. The app reminds you.
help.when-to-change.note1: Changing any of them signs out the other devices it had opened.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.title: When something goes wrong: how it is decided
help.when-something-goes-wrong.summary: Where a person pays SeeBuyGet first for a load, the driver is paid 24 hours after delivery. A problem reported in those 24 hours is decided by a protocol: three questions answered from what was recorded, the same for everybody — the person who paid, the receiver, the driver, and the shops and hubs it passed. Never more than the carriage price goes back.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.step1: Send app, within 24 hours of delivery: My parcels, open the load under “Your loads”, or the parcel brought to your door, then “Report a problem”. Choose what is wrong — damaged, part missing, not received, not what was sent — say what you found, and add a photo of it. The driver’s pay stays held.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.step2: Driver app: the load is shown under My loads › “Problems reported”. Answer once: what you saw when you took it over and at the door, with a photo of your own if you have one. Your answer is shown beside the report.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.step3: Question 1 — was it handed over with the delivery code, or did the sender say it arrived? If not, it was not delivered: the carriage price goes back to the person who paid, and the driver is not paid.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.step4: Question 2 — was the same problem noted at the door, when the receiver took it? If not, the driver is paid: what is found after the handover, such as damage hidden inside the packing, is for the damage claim report and the person’s own insurer.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.step5: Question 3 — was the same problem noted when the driver took it over? If so, it was so before, and the driver is paid. If not, it happened while the driver had it: the carriage price goes back to the person who paid, and the driver is not paid for that load.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.note1: A member of SeeBuyGet staff confirms what the protocol says with one tap. Going against it takes a written reason and a second member of staff, and both sides are shown that reason.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.note2: Everybody is told the outcome in their own app, with the step that decided it — never by text message. With nothing reported in the 24 hours, the driver is paid then.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.note3: Why a protocol: a decision read from the record, the same every time, can be explained to everybody who made the load move, and nobody depends on one person’s judgement on the day.
help.when-something-goes-wrong.note4: The carriage price is the most that goes back. Goods themselves are paid for only by a company that has stated cover, and none has yet: the damage claim report is for your own insurer.
help.parcel-from-abroad.title: A parcel from abroad: who does what, and who pays
help.parcel-from-abroad.summary: Where SeeBuyGet runs a route between two countries, a shop can take in a parcel for a shop in the other one. The sender pays to the arrival airport; customs there releases it or asks for duty; the receiver pays what customs asks to the clearing agent, and our clearance fee and the last leg at their shop.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step1: At the sending shop: the shop opens the parcel with you, checks what is inside, photographs it and the invoice or receipt, and seals it in front of you. It writes down what is inside, how many items, the value from the invoice, and the sender’s and the receiver’s names as on their ID.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step2: You pay at the counter, in cash: the route’s price for its size, with the shop’s fee and ours, and the tax. The shop prints the label, with the seal and the two airports on it, and the customs papers, which go in the pouch on the parcel.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step3: It goes to the route’s departure hub, where it is handed to the route’s carrier, a forwarder or haulier, under the carrier’s reference. The carrier takes it to SeeBuyGet’s customs warehouse at the arrival airport.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step4: At the warehouse, customs decides. Released, it goes on to the receiver’s shop. Held, customs asks for import duty and tax, and the parcel stays at the warehouse until that is paid.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step5: Held: the receiver is told in the Send app what customs asks, its reference, who to pay it to (the clearing agent) and by when, 14 days on. Paid and released, it goes on. Not paid by then, it goes back to the sender, who is asked what to do with it and pays for the way back.
help.parcel-from-abroad.step6: At the receiver’s shop: the receiver gives the code the sender passed on and pays our clearance fee and the last leg, in cash. The shop is told the amount before it asks for the code.
help.parcel-from-abroad.note1: Why every parcel is declared: goods carried for others are not anybody’s personal belongings, so a parcel is declared whatever its value. SeeBuyGet never chooses a tariff code or works out duty: that is customs’ and the clearing agent’s.
help.parcel-from-abroad.note2: Nothing of customs’ money passes through SeeBuyGet: the duty is paid to the clearing agent. Each country decides who collects it and how our part is paid; everywhere today, it is the clearing agent and at collection.
help.parcel-from-abroad.note3: Without a signal, a parcel abroad is not taken in: its price, its route and its customs papers come from SeeBuyGet while the sender is at the counter.
help.parcel-from-abroad.note4: SeeBuyGet sends no text about a parcel: the receiver and the sender are told everything in the Send app’s notices.
help.connect-your-shop.title: Connect a webshop to SeeBuyGet: for developers
help.connect-your-shop.summary: What a store’s developer does to connect its webshop or shop system: show pickup shops and prices at the checkout, create a shipment for each order, and hear every step of the parcel. Build against test keys first: nothing is created or billed until the store’s live keys are used.
help.connect-your-shop.step1: Ask the store owner for the store ID, and make the keys together in the Store app, under “Store › Connect your shop system”. A key is made only when somebody asks for it, and a secret one is shown once: copy it into your password manager straight away.
help.connect-your-shop.step2: Build against test keys first (“Make a key › Test”): every check runs, nothing is created and nothing is billed.
help.connect-your-shop.step3: Prices and pickup shops at the checkout: a publishable key (“Make a key › In a page”) may sit in your product page or on the shipping button. It asks for prices and pickup shops, POST /v1/sbg/shipping/quotes, and can do nothing else.
help.connect-your-shop.step4: A shipment for each order, from your server: send the secret key in the X-SBG-Key header and POST /v1/sbg/shipping/shipments with the buyer’s phone, the price you quoted (quoteId) or the two ends and the parcel’s size, a photo of the contents (uploaded first to /v1/sbg/shipping/photos), and your own order reference. The answer is the parcel; its label is at /v1/sbg/shipping/shipments/{id}/label.
help.connect-your-shop.step5: Every step of the parcel, told to your system: the owner sets your order-update address in the Store app. Each message is a POST with a short JSON body (event, data, at). It is signed with the store’s signing secret: the x-sbg-signature header is an HMAC-SHA256 of the body, which you check before you trust a message. x-sbg-delivery is the same on every try, so a repeat can be skipped. Answer 200 to say you took it.
help.connect-your-shop.step6: Going live: the owner makes the live keys, and you put them in place of the test ones. Then send a test message from the Store app and check it arrives under “Messages to your own system”.
help.connect-your-shop.note1: Never put a secret key or the signing secret in a web page, or in an app a buyer downloads: they belong on your server only.
help.connect-your-shop.note2: A lost secret cannot be shown again: the owner replaces it in the Store app, and the old one stops working at once.
help.connect-your-shop.note3: Whether the buyer’s collection code rides in the ready_for_pickup message is the store’s choice, in the Store app. Buyers also see it in their own Send app.
